solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spanish hero holding up boy with arrow

indicators.note: holding says the Spanish hero's name wraps around the next piece

parts.note: El Cid is the medieval Spanish hero
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish champion supports a young archer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is pictured as a winged child with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Insurance, perhaps, about ended

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
something ended is over

explanation.surface: An insurance policy is described as having roughly expired.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance protection is commonly called cover; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Disguise picture of exile, apt to stray

indicators.note: letters made to stray wander out of their order and settle in a new one

explanation.surface: An exile's photograph is blurred, liable to go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters blur a face into coarse blocks to hide identity, which is exactly this verb.

clue.text: Martial arts expert going to church ball

parts.note: a dan is a black-belt grade in judo or karate, and a holder of it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A karate master heads off to a church social.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social event for dancing.

clue.text: This season's match? Er, miss it, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters have come out wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A seasonal football fixture is hesitantly regretted: someone will have to skip it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' after 'season' stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive period at the end of December is the season the surface refers to.

clue.text: A Romeo brings up something outstanding

parts.note: R is Romeo in the phonetic alphabet
to bring up children is to rear them

explanation.surface: A lover from Shakespeare raises a remarkable matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Debts still unpaid after their due date are money outstanding.

clue.text: Greek character turning up in temperate zones

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Greek person appears in mild climates.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the letters bottom to top; 'in' marks them as tucked inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in that script.

clue.text: Composer's art's reflected by American symphony primarily

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the letters of art's are read backwards

parts.note: art's read as the plural arts

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of symphony

explanation.surface: A composer's work is mirrored in an American symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss and Richard Strauss were both famous composers.

clue.text: Hateful, earthborn eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd mortal is detestable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent inspires loathing, so it is hateful in the sense of detestable.

clue.text: Spiteful woman from NE14 returned

indicators.note: returned says those letters are read back to front

parts.note: read NE plus 14 in Roman numerals, XIV

explanation.surface: A nasty woman comes back from a London-style postcode.
explanation.walkthrough: NE14 looks like a postcode, but 14 must become the Roman numeral XIV.
explanation.definitionFit: A female fox gives its name to an ill-tempered, quarrelsome woman.

clue.text: In furniture store, stop arranging one's bloomers!

indicators.note: In places the stop word inside the store's name

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture retailer
to ban something is to stop it

explanation.surface: Someone in a furniture shop is told to stop sorting their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of flower arranging; bloomers here are things that bloom.

clue.text: Waves you might have in your hair?

definitions.text: you might have in your hair?
definitions.meaning: curlers set in hair while it dries

explanation.surface: Waves of the sea, or waves set in a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Long swelling ocean breakers and hair curlers share this name.

clue.text: Country's voters for 4? Hardly!

definitions.meaning: the nation's, with the apostrophe s
the saying that these birds would never vote for the festive season named at 4 down, when they are eaten

explanation.surface: A nation's electorate would hardly back the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'like turkeys voting for Christmas' means backing something against your own interest.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation of Ankara plus 's, and the birds that are roasted at the festive dinner.

clue.text: No aliens could get near them

indicators.note: could get suggests the letters can be turned into something new

explanation.surface: Extraterrestrials can't approach humans.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of our own planet are by definition not beings from other worlds.

clue.text: Cross, see, after drinking port up

indicators.note: drinking means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: to spy is to see

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy after drinking port.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and argumentative, i.e. angry.

clue.text: Celebrations as vicar goes on the Spanish railway

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A vicar's party trip on a Spanish train.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is noisy merrymaking, the activity of festivities.

clue.text: Yonder is a woman

parts.note: yonder means over there
is shortened to 's

explanation.surface: Pointing out a woman in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of Mother Teresa or Theresa May, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Sadly, pulpit's come apart

indicators.note: sadly suggests something has gone wrong with the letters, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church pulpit has unfortunately fallen to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or break into pieces; the phrasal verb means to divide.

clue.text: Doctor and duke tied up

parts.note: to doctor a drink is to lace it

explanation.surface: A physician and a nobleman are bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb, to spike, not a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes are fastened by threading and tying their cords.

clue.text: Bread is mine: thanks!

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Someone claims a loaf and says thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat Middle Eastern loaf, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Stuff above re-attempted in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Material noted earlier was tried once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat too much.

clue.text: Heads of European governments with outsize conceits

indicators.note: heads of picks the first letter of each following word

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: European leaders have outsized vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two words lose all but their heads; OS is a standard label for extra-large clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceits here are self-images and vanities, plural senses of self-esteem.

clue.text: Soldier in charge encountered traveller in space

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A commanding officer met an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy body orbiting the Sun journeys through space.

clue.text: Schedule for lightweight: yours truly!

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a gram is a tiny unit of weight
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A timetable for a boxer at the lightest weight: the writer himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned list of events or broadcasts is a timetable.

clue.text: An agreement to return to see girl

indicators.note: to return means the letters run back the other way

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: An agreement to come back and visit a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for lady, used as a girl's name.
